summary: Turkish family foundry (380 staff, EUR 15.8 M) in distress: restructuring, bank watching monthly, half the shop floor idle, second shift on hold. We are 3.2 % of its turnover. Pump housing HB 40 is 60/40 with active co-source 70190, so we can shift volume. Red scorecard four quarters running (OTD 52 %, 2652 ppm). Owner offered open-book costing. Trade volume and faster payment for price; past renewals settled 2.6-3.8 pts below its ask.
notes: Needs cash and work for idle shifts; repeatedly asks 10-day payment. Fears margin loss ('cannot sign anything that lowers our margin') and losing HB 40 share to 70190. Price is 19 % under a German-cost should-cost, not its own plant, so no proof it is below its cost. Invited to the HX 80-200 RFQ (per 70120 file).

evidence.quote: the bank is watching every month. 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.'
half the shop floor was idle, two shifts are on short hours
they could take additional parts at short notice; the second shift has been on hold since spring.
he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.

levers: binding volume to fill second shift
arguments: quality record: red four quarters, OTD 52 %, 2652 ppm
its own cost shares from the offered open book
volume shift to active co-source 70190 (it is dearer at 43.39, no rival-price argument)
binding volume / forecast fills idle capacity
avoid: a bare margin cut with nothing in return
changing terms after its final offer
tactics: Accept its open-book offer: ask for hourly rates and material shares, then argue from them.
Lead with the red scorecard; OTD 52 % is far below the 95 % target.
Offer extra HB 40 quota from 70190 as a binding volume for a visible price step.
Offer 10-14 day payment only against price; cash is its main need.
Frame the deal as cash plus volume, not as a margin cut.
playbook.expected_concession: No arena data; past renewals settled 2.6-3.8 pts below its ask (2024: asked +3.0 %, settled 0 %).
